hooks.text: A single storm on Saturn can wrap around the entire planet.
Saturn looks peaceful, but one storm can swallow the entire planet.
Every thirty years, an Earth-sized storm wraps entirely around Saturn.

title: The Storm That Bit Its Own Tail
description: Saturn periodically generates an Earth-sized thunderstorm so immense its tail wraps around the entire planet.

beats.text: Every thirty years, the gas giant erupts with a colossal Great White Spot.

beats.text: Six of these planetary tempests have been recorded since eighteen seventy-six.

beats.text: In twenty-ten, NASA's Cassini spacecraft watched a storm head grow as wide as Earth.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft image showing the Earth-sized storm head on Saturn, 2011

beats.text: This monster generated ten lightning flashes per second while whipping out a massive tail.
beats.visual: False-color Cassini image showing convective clouds and lightning regions, 2011
queries: Cassini Saturn storm radio plasma discharge

beats.text: Within six months, that tail stretched around the world until it hit its own head.
